title: Learning to Communicate with Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
how_tested: RIAL and DIAL methods for learning communication protocols in communication riddles and multi-agent vision tasks under partial observability
finding: Agents learned end-to-end communication protocols from scratch; differentiable inter-agent learning (centralized training, decentralized execution) was key.

title: Multi-Agent Cooperation and the Emergence of (Natural) Language
how_tested: Neural sender-receiver referential games on images
finding: Agents develop a shared communication protocol from scratch, and environment tweaks make word meanings align better with human semantics.

title: Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning in Sequential Social Dilemmas
how_tested: Gathering game: an agent hit twice by another's beam is removed from the game for N_tagged frames; N_tagged and apple abundance are manipulated.
finding: Beam use (aggression) rises with scarcity and falls with higher conflict cost (partial: removal is a competitive attack, not a sanction for norm violation).

title: Maintaining cooperation in complex social dilemmas using deep reinforcement learning
how_tested: Constructs approximate Markov tit-for-tat (amTFT) deep-RL agents that are nice, provokable and forgiving in Markov social dilemmas.
finding: Generalized TFT agents maintain cooperation in complex environments, theoretically and experimentally.

title: Emergence of Grounded Compositional Language in Multi-Agent Populations
how_tested: Multi-agent RL in a grounded physical environment with discrete symbol channels
finding: Populations of agents develop a basic grounded compositional language, plus non-verbal pointing and guiding when communication is restricted.

title: A multi-agent reinforcement learning model of common-pool resource appropriation
how_tested: Independent deep RL agents in a partially observed common-pool resource Markov game (with a tag-out beam)
finding: Emergent exclusion and territoriality arise among independent learners, linking exclusion, sustainability and inequality.

title: Adaptive Mechanism Design: Learning to Promote Cooperation
how_tested: An external planning agent learns to hand out extra rewards and punishments to independent learners in matrix social dilemmas, anticipating their parameter updates.
finding: Learners reach high-welfare cooperation; the planner learns that punishing defection is cheaper than rewarding cooperation, and the incentives it has to pay fall toward zero over time.

title: Emergent Communication through Negotiation
how_tested: RL agents negotiate with an ungrounded cheap-talk channel alongside a grounded proposal channel; self-interested and prosocial agents are compared.
finding: Self-interested agents did not use the cheap-talk channel effectively, while prosocial agents learned to use it.

title: Emergent Tool Use From Multi-Agent Autocurricula
how_tested: Large-scale multi-agent RL in team hide-and-seek
finding: Competition yields an autocurriculum of six emergent strategy phases involving coordinated team tool use (shelter building, ramp use).

title: Biases for Emergent Communication in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
how_tested: Inductive biases (positive signalling, positive listening) for decentralized learners in a one-step game and a temporally extended environment
finding: The biases eased the joint exploration problem so communication emerged without centralized training, improving performance.

title: Learning Reciprocity in Complex Sequential Social Dilemmas
how_tested: Online RL algorithm with reciprocal behaviour toward co-players in a 2-player Markov game and 5-player intertemporal social dilemmas alongside selfish learners.
finding: Reciprocating agents induce pro-social outcomes for the wider group.

title: Social Influence as Intrinsic Motivation for Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
how_tested: Counterfactual causal-influence intrinsic reward in sequential social dilemmas (Cleanup, Harvest), with and without an explicit communication channel
finding: Rewarding influence over others improved coordination and cooperation in social dilemmas and produced more meaningful emergent communication protocols.

title: On the Pitfalls of Measuring Emergent Communication
how_tested: Deep RL agents in matrix games with a communication channel; comparison of emergent-communication metrics (e.g., positive signalling vs. positive listening, causal influence)
finding: Agents can appear to communicate by common metrics while messages have no effect on others; recommends causal-influence measures.

title: Evolving intrinsic motivations for altruistic behavior
how_tested: Deep RL agents in intertemporal social dilemmas with a modular architecture whose intrinsic-reward module evolves under multi-level (group) selection.
finding: Evolved intrinsic motivations produce cooperative inductive biases, learned model-free.

title: Partner Selection for the Emergence of Cooperation in Multi-Agent Systems Using Reinforcement Learning
how_tested: RL agents in an iterated PD population can choose interaction partners (partner selection) vs. random matching.
finding: With partner selection, selfish learners learn to retaliate against defectors and cooperate with others, yielding a prosocial society.

title: The Emergence of Adversarial Communication in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
how_tested: Graph-neural-network communication among a cooperative team plus a self-interested agent sharing a differentiable channel
finding: A self-interested agent learned adversarial (manipulative) communication that degraded the team, and the team could adapt to filter it.

title: Compositionality and Generalization in Emergent Languages
how_tested: Sender-receiver games with new disentanglement-inspired compositionality metrics; generalization and transmission to new learners tested
finding: With large input spaces emergent languages generalize, but compositionality does not predict generalization; more compositional languages are easier for new learners to acquire.

title: Model-free conventions in multi-agent reinforcement learning with heterogeneous preferences
how_tested: Model-free MARL in a spatially extended collective-action game (Allelopathic Harvest) where subgroups prefer different equilibria
finding: Complex, large-scale conventions emerged from model-free (habit-like) learning despite heterogeneous preferences, with free-riding and start-up problems.

title: Emergent Multi-Agent Communication in the Deep Learning Era
how_tested: survey
finding: Reviews deep-learning emergent communication among agent communities, framing scientific (language evolution) and applied (interactive AI) goals.

title: Gifting in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (Student Abstract)
how_tested: RL agents in a Harvest common-pool resource environment get a gifting action that transfers reward to other agents.
finding: Gifting can greatly improve learning progress in the resource-appropriation setting (preliminary student abstract).

title: Learning to Incentivize Other Learning Agents
how_tested: Each RL agent learns an incentive function to give rewards directly to other agents, accounting for its effect on their learning, in social dilemmas (e.g., Escape Room, Cleanup).
finding: Learned peer incentives beat standard RL and often reach a near-optimal division of labor. This is peer-to-peer reward, not a central subsidy.

title: Cooperation and Reputation Dynamics with Reinforcement Learning
how_tested: Q-learners in indirect-reciprocity donation games must learn both to use and to assign reputations; interventions: seeding fixed agents and introspection-based intrinsic rewards.
finding: Plain Q-learning often converges to bad equilibria; combining both interventions stabilizes reputation-based cooperation even when fully decentralized.

title: Multi-Agent Curricula and Emergent Implicit Signaling
authors: Niko A. Grupen, Daniel D. Lee and Bart Selman
how_tested: Curriculum-trained decentralized pursuers in pursuit-evasion; information exchange measured via position-based social influence
finding: Pursuers learned implicit (non-verbal) signaling and exchanged more than twice as much information as baselines, relying on it to coordinate.

title: A multi-agent reinforcement learning model of reputation and cooperation in human groups
how_tested: Clean Up public-goods task with identifiable vs anonymous conditions, run with humans and with MARL agents given an intrinsic reputation motive.
finding: Humans cooperate only when identifiable; the MARL model with reputation motivation reproduces this and develops turn-taking coordination (partial: artificial-agent arm is a model of human data).

title: Emergent Social Learning via Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
how_tested: Independent RL agents in a shared environment with experts; tests whether agents learn to imitate/learn from others, with a model-based auxiliary loss.
finding: Vanilla model-free agents do not use social learning, but with environment constraints and auxiliary loss they learn from experts and outperform solo-trained agents.

title: Emergent Communication under Competition
how_tested: Modified sender-receiver game spanning degrees of partial competition, standard RL learners
finding: Communication emerged in partially competitive settings, in proportion to the degree of cooperation; distinguishes communication from manipulation.

title: Emergent Prosociality in Multi-Agent Games Through Gifting
how_tested: Self-interested learning agents in multi-equilibrium (high-risk coordination) games may transfer part of their reward to peers; analysed with dynamical-systems theory and simulations.
finding: Gifting enlarged the basins of attraction of prosocial equilibria and substantially improved convergence to them without external reward shaping.

title: Melting Pot 2.0
how_tested: Benchmark scenarios test focal MARL agents against reciprocator background bots (e.g., Coins high-/low-threshold reciprocators that defect for 100-150 steps after mismatching coins; Clean Up conditional cleaners).
finding: Provides standardized tests of how focal populations respond to conditional-cooperation partners (benchmark; no single mechanism effect reported).

title: Emergent Communication at Scale
how_tested: Referential games scaled on dataset size, task complexity and population size; voting and imitation methods for leveraging populations
finding: Larger populations did not automatically yield more robust protocols; topographic similarity was a poor metric on natural images, and ease-of-learning/transfer were more informative.

title: Formal Contracts Mitigate Social Dilemmas in Multi-Agent RL
venue: arXiv; AAMAS 2023 as 'Get It in Writing: Formal Contracts Mitigate Social Dilemmas in Multi-Agent RL'
how_tested: Markov games are augmented so agents can voluntarily agree to binding, pre-specified conditional reward transfers (MOCA training), tested on static games, traffic, pollution and common-pool resource domains.
finding: With a rich enough contract space all subgame-perfect equilibria are socially optimal, and contracting raises welfare empirically. Transfers can act as pre-agreed penalties but are not framed as breach penalties, so partial.

title: Emergent Bartering Behaviour in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
how_tested: MARL agents produce, trade and consume resources in a spatial microeconomy; supply/demand shifts manipulated
finding: Emergent prices responded to supply and demand as microeconomics predicts, varied over space, and some agents specialized as traders arbitraging between regions.

title: Spurious normativity enhances learning of compliance and enforcement behavior in artificial agents
how_tested: MARL agents in a foraging environment learn to punish peers who eat taboo berries; an extra 'silly rule' taboo on a harmless berry is added as a manipulation.
finding: Peer punishment helps agents avoid poisonous berries, and the silly rule further improves returns by giving agents more practice at enforcement.

title: On the role of population heterogeneity in emergent communication
how_tested: Lewis signaling game with varying population size and speaker/listener learning-speed heterogeneity
finding: Population size alone did not yield more structured language; emergent language properties depended on the relative learning speeds of speakers and listeners, and modeling heterogeneity recovered the sociolinguistic group-size effect.

title: The AI Economist: Taxation policy design via two-level deep multiagent reinforcement learning
how_tested: A planner learns tax schedules with redistribution while a population of RL economic agents co-adapts (two-level deep RL).
finding: Learned tax policies improve the equality-productivity trade-off over baselines despite tax-gaming. The setting is an economy rather than a social dilemma, so partial for P04-02.

title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors
how_tested: Multi-agent LLM framework (expert recruitment, collaborative decision-making, execution, evaluation) on reasoning, coding, tool-use and Minecraft tasks; qualitative analysis of group behaviors
finding: Groups outperformed single agents, and volunteer, conformity and destructive behaviors emerged among agents during collaboration.

title: Investigating the Impact of Direct Punishment on the Emergence of Cooperation in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Systems
venue: Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Systems 39, article 19 (2025)
how_tested: MARL populations in social dilemmas with direct punishment, third-party punishment, partner selection and reputation, alone and combined.
finding: Direct punishment supports cooperation, and its effect depends on how it combines with third-party punishment, partner selection and reputation.

title: Emergence of Scale-Free Networks in Social Interactions among Large Language Models
authors: Giordano De Marzo, Luciano Pietronero and David Garcia
how_tested: Generative agents (GPT-3.5-turbo) choose whom to follow in a growing network; manipulation of agent names to remove token priors
finding: Agents produced scale-free follow networks, but token-prior bias could yield extreme centralization; renaming agents removed the bias and produced a range of realistic networks.

title: S$^3$: Social-network Simulation System with Large Language Model-Empowered Agents
how_tested: LLM agents (prompt engineering + prompt tuning) initialized from real social-network data simulate emotion, attitude and interaction; individual- and population-level predictions compared with real data (gender discrimination, nuclear energy scenarios)
finding: Population-level propagation of information, attitudes and emotions emerged from agent interactions and tracked real-world dynamics with reasonable accuracy.

title: Emergent Resource Exchange and Tolerated Theft Behavior using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
how_tested: MARL foraging environment with a campfire congregation period; agents can drop and pick up resources
finding: A resource-exchange protocol emerged; agents learned to avoid being cheated by partners but not always by third parties, and tolerated-theft-like behavior appeared.

title: MRL-PoS: A Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning based Proof of Stake Consensus Algorithm for Blockchain
how_tested: A PoS consensus design in which MARL agents (nodes) receive rewards and penalties to push out malicious validators and reward honest ones.
finding: The abstract reports that the reward/penalty system removes malicious nodes. It is a blockchain security design, not a cooperation study, and does not report stake-slashing manipulation in detail, so partial.

title: Learning to Participate through Trading of Reward Shares
how_tested: Independently trained RL agents in general-sum Markov games / social dilemmas can buy equity-like shares in other agents' rewards (stock-market-inspired mechanism).
finding: Holding shares in others' returns led agents to cooperate and, in extended domains, to specialize and divide subtasks. This is partial evidence: tradable reward shares are only an analogue of worker-cooperative ownership.

title: EconAgent: Large Language Model-Empowered Agents for Simulating Macroeconomic Activities
how_tested: LLM household agents with perception/memory/reflection decide work and consumption in a macroeconomic environment with rule-based tax and central bank
finding: Aggregate simulations reproduced macroeconomic regularities (e.g., Phillips curve, Okun's law) more reasonably than rule-based or RL agent baselines.

title: Consensus-based Participatory Budgeting for Legitimacy: Decision Support via Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
venue: LOD 2023 (Machine Learning, Optimization, and Data Science)
how_tested: MARL voter agents interact to reach compromises in participatory budgeting using real PB data from Poland, compared against standard voting aggregation rules.
finding: Agents reach consensus efficiently and robustly, framed as increasing legitimacy of PB outcomes.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
how_tested: 25-agent sandbox town (Smallville) simulation with memory/reflection/planning architecture; ablations and human believability evaluation
finding: From a single seeded intention, agents autonomously diffused information, formed relationships and coordinated a group event (Valentine's party), showing emergent social behavior in a small generative-agent society.

title: Modeling Moral Choices in Social Dilemmas with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
how_tested: RL agents with intrinsic rewards encoding different moral frameworks (consequentialist vs norm-based) interact in Prisoner's Dilemma, Volunteer's Dilemma and Stag Hunt.
finding: Different internalised moral reward types produce different patterns of cooperation, defection and exploitation among agents.

title: Deconstructing Cooperation and Ostracism via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
how_tested: Two RL agents play repeated PD, each with a cooperation policy and a network-rewiring (connect/disconnect) policy.
finding: Rewiring facilitates cooperation via learned ostracism of defectors, but ostracism emerges from and then reinforces cooperation rather than causing it alone.

title: A learning agent that acquires social norms from public sanctions in decentralized multi-agent settings
how_tested: Decentralized RL agents see all public sanctioning events; the architecture includes a classifier of approved/disapproved behavior and a motivation to punish in step with the group.
finding: Agents acquire beneficial sanctioning norms that reduce free-riding and raise per-agent returns.

title: Resolving social dilemmas with minimal reward transfer
how_tested: Defines a 'general self-interest level' and computes minimal reward-transfer structures that make the social optimum dominant in multi-player social dilemmas.
finding: Minimal reward redistribution can align individual and group incentives; the work is mostly analytical, so partial.

title: Exploring Large Language Models for Communication Games: An Empirical Study on Werewolf
how_tested: Frozen LLM agents with retrieval and reflection play multi-player Werewolf; qualitative analysis of strategic behavior
finding: Strategic behaviors not specified in prompts emerged, including trust, confrontation, camouflage and leadership.

title: The emergence of division of labor through decentralized social sanctioning
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 2023
how_tested: Lifetime-learning self-interested agents choose roles with unequal payoffs; model of decentralized social sanctioning that redistributes rewards
finding: Without sanctioning, critical low-paying roles went unfilled; emergent decentralized sanctioning norms enabled a productive division of labor covering all critical roles.

title: Project Sid: Many-agent simulations toward AI civilization
how_tested: 10-1000+ LLM agents (PIANO architecture) in Minecraft societies with civilizational benchmarks
finding: Agents autonomously developed specialized roles, adhered to and changed collective rules, and transmitted cultural and religious memes.

title: Simulating Opinion Dynamics with Networks of LLM-based Agents
how_tested: Networks of LLM agents discussing scientific topics, with and without induced confirmation bias
finding: LLM agents converge toward scientifically accurate consensus by default; inducing confirmation bias produces opinion fragmentation consistent with classical ABMs.

title: AI agents can coordinate beyond human scale
authors: Giordano De Marzo, Claudio Castellano and David Garcia
how_tested: Groups of LLM agents repeatedly coordinate on an arbitrary binary choice; opinion dynamics fitted with a majority-force coefficient across group sizes and models
finding: LLM groups spontaneously reached consensus via majority-following; the majority force declines with group size, giving a critical group size that grows exponentially with language ability and exceeds typical human group sizes for top models.

title: Algorithmic Collusion by Large Language Models
how_tested: Repeated oligopoly pricing and auction experiments with LLM pricing agents; prompt variations
finding: LLM pricing agents quickly and autonomously reach supracompetitive prices, with innocuous prompt phrasing strongly affecting the degree of collusion.

title: AgentGroupChat: An Interactive Group Chat Simulacra For Better Eliciting Emergent Behavior
how_tested: LLM characters (Verbal Strategist Agent) in four group-chat narrative scenarios; evaluation of human-alignment and emergence of collective behavior
finding: Collective behaviors (group consensus, self-sacrificing concessions) emerged when environments allowed extensive information exchange and characters had diverse traits and strategic adaptability.

title: Embodied LLM Agents Learn to Cooperate in Organized Teams
how_tested: Embodied LLM agent teams with prompt-imposed organization structures (with/without designated leader), human-agent collaboration, and LLM-generated organizational prompts via Criticize-Reflect
finding: Designated leadership improved team efficiency, agents displayed leadership qualities and spontaneous cooperative behavior, and LLM-proposed organization structures reduced communication cost (structure partly imposed, partly agent-designed).

title: Evolution of Social Norms in LLM Agents using Natural Language
authors: Ilya Horiguchi, Takahide Yoshida, Takashi Ikegami
how_tested: Seven GPT-4 agents with prompted vengefulness/boldness traits play a modified Axelrod norms game (test/cheat/punish actions plus a natural-language discussion phase) and are observed for norm and metanorm emergence.
finding: Agents spontaneously produced metanorm-like enforcement through dialogue (the abstract reports norms enforcing punishment of those who do not punish cheating; the body also describes agents punishing punishers deemed disruptive), and groups with moderate vengefulness and boldness were most stable. Evidence is qualitative/emergent, not a manipulated metanorm condition.

title: Principal-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Orchestrating AI Agents with Contracts
how_tested: A learning principal designs outcome-contingent payment contracts for learning agents under hidden action (moral hazard), tested on random binary game trees and a multi-agent Coin Game.
finding: The meta-algorithm converges to subgame-perfect equilibrium contracts. PARTIAL: these are moral-hazard incentive contracts, not risk- or history-based premiums.

title: Strategic Collusion of LLM Agents: Market Division in Multi-Commodity Competitions
how_tested: Multi-commodity Cournot competition with LLM agents
finding: LLM agents divide markets and monopolize commodities without explicit collusion instructions.

title: Secret Collusion among AI Agents: Multi-Agent Deception via Steganography
how_tested: Formal threat model plus model evaluation framework (CASE) measuring steganographic capabilities of frontier LLMs
finding: Frontier LLMs show rising capability for steganographic covert communication that could enable undetectable collusion against overseers.

title: Learning and Sustaining Shared Normative Systems via Bayesian Rule Induction in Markov Games
how_tested: Agents assume a shared normative system and infer norms by Bayesian rule induction from others' compliance and sanctions in Markov games (resource management, labour compensation).
finding: Newcomers rapidly adopt established norms and groups converge on shared norms that sustain cooperative institutions, with far less experience than model-free norm learning.

title: Network Formation and Dynamics Among Multi-LLMs
how_tested: Multiple LLM agents make link-formation decisions in synthetic and real-world (friendship, telecom, employment) networks; benchmarked against human decisions
finding: LLM agents reproduced preferential attachment, triadic closure and homophily and macro properties such as community structure and small-world effects, with context-dependent emphasis (homophily vs. heterophily).

title: Cultural evolution in populations of Large Language Models
how_tested: Open-source framework for multi-agent LLM cultural-evolution simulations varying network structure, personality and social-information aggregation/transformation; example experiments
finding: Provides a manipulable testbed for machine cultural evolution, showing that population structure and transmission settings shape how cultural content changes over generations.

title: When LLMs Play the Telephone Game: Cultural Attractors as Conceptual Tools to Evaluate LLMs in Multi-turn Settings
how_tested: Transmission-chain (telephone game) experiments with iterated LLM rewriting, measuring toxicity, positivity, difficulty and length drift
finding: Small per-step biases compound over transmission chains so text evolves toward model-specific cultural attractor states.

title: Emergent Language: A Survey and Taxonomy
how_tested: survey
finding: Surveys and taxonomizes emergent-language research in MARL, including prerequisites for emergence and metrics for its success.

title: A memory-based spatial evolutionary game with the dynamic interaction between learners and profiteers
how_tested: Spatial evolutionary game where 'profiteers' imitate highest-payoff neighbours via the Fermi rule and 'learners' use Q-learning, with Markov role switching and payoff memory.
finding: Interaction between Fermi imitators and Q-learners fosters cooperation; memory helps profiteers cooperate and higher learning rates increase cooperators.

title: Cooperate or Collapse: Emergence of Sustainable Cooperation in a Society of LLM Agents
how_tested: GovSim common-pool simulation with five LLM agents; a moderator publicly discloses each agent's previous-round harvest (transparent harvest reporting) before a free-form discussion phase.
finding: Most LLMs fail to sustain the resource; communication matters (overuse +22% without it). Transparency is a fixed feature, not manipulated.

title: Emergent Dominance Hierarchies in Reinforcement Learning Agents
how_tested: Populations of RL agents in a repeated aggression/submission setting analyzed with ethological dominance-hierarchy measures; transfer to new populations
finding: Without explicit programming or intrinsic rewards, agents invented, enforced and transmitted dominance hierarchies resembling those in animal groups.

title: Emergence of Social Norms in Generative Agent Societies: Principles and Architecture
how_tested: CRSEC architecture (norm creation, spreading, evaluation, compliance) for LLM generative agents in the Smallville sandbox.
finding: Social norms emerge and social conflicts fall relative to agents without the architecture, supported by a 30-person human evaluation.

title: Y Social: an LLM-powered Social Media Digital Twin
how_tested: Platform paper: LLM-driven agents post, comment, follow and react on a simulated microblogging platform (Y) with configurable recommender and platform policies; example analyses of generated data
finding: Introduces a social-media digital twin in which content dissemination, engagement and network dynamics emerge from LLM agent interactions, intended for studying emergent online phenomena and platform-policy effects.

title: Normative Modules: A Generative Agent Architecture for Learning Norms that Supports Multi-Agent Cooperation
how_tested: LLM generative agents with a normative module must identify which of several institutions the group treats as authoritative (and ignore non-authoritative ones) and coordinate sanctioning accordingly.
finding: Agents with the normative module achieve more stable cooperative outcomes than baseline generative agents without it.

title: Spontaneous Emergence of Agent Individuality through Social Interactions in LLM-Based Communities
how_tested: Group simulation of initially undifferentiated LLM agents communicating in natural language on a grid
finding: Individual personalities, memories and social norms and cooperation differentiate spontaneously from identical agents through interaction.

title: Cultural Evolution of Cooperation among LLM Agents
how_tested: Iterated Donor Game over generations of LLM agents who can observe recipients' recent behaviour; optional costly-punishment variant.
finding: Cooperation evolution differs by base model (Claude 3.5 Sonnet > Gemini 1.5 Flash > GPT-4o); only Claude used costly punishment to raise scores; high seed sensitivity.

title: Decoding Echo Chambers: LLM-Powered Simulations Revealing Polarization in Social Networks
how_tested: LLM-agent opinion networks on three network structures with recommendation algorithms; mitigation strategies
finding: LLM agent networks reproduce echo chamber and polarization dynamics, and active/passive nudges can mitigate them.

title: Shall We Team Up: Exploring Spontaneous Cooperation of Competing LLM Agents
how_tested: Three competitive simulation scenarios (per the paper, including a Bertrand-style market) without explicit cooperation instructions
finding: Cooperation gradually emerges among competing LLM agents in line with human behavioral data.

title: Get It Cooperating: Enhancing Generative Agent Cooperation with Commitment Devices
how_tested: LLM agents given commitment devices in Prisoner's Dilemma, Public Goods, and a dynamic Harvest game.
finding: Agents used commitment devices to reach the socially optimal (new) equilibrium in simple games, but gains were limited in the complex dynamic Harvest game.
located_via: opened page (ML Anthology mirror https://mlanthology.org/icmlw/2024/yan2024icmlw-get/; OpenReview blocked by bot check)

title: OASIS: Open Agent Social Interaction Simulations with One Million Agents
how_tested: Social-media simulator (X/Reddit-like) with up to 1M LLM agents, recommender systems and dynamic networks
finding: LLM agent populations replicate information spreading, group polarization and herd effects, with herd behavior stronger than in humans and group dynamics intensifying with scale.

title: Evolution of cooperation in the public goods game with Q-learning
how_tested: Spatial public goods game on a lattice with Q-learning agents, compared against the Fermi imitation-rule baseline, with and without voluntary participation.
finding: Cooperation emerges more readily under Q-learning than under Fermi imitation; voluntary participation produces a non-monotonic dependence of cooperation.

title: Fair Compromises in Participatory Budgeting: a Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
how_tested: Multi-agent deep RL voters (branching network architecture) learn voting strategies in participatory budgeting.
finding: Fair compromises emerge, especially when projects have smaller costs.

title: Evaluating LLM Agent Collusion in Double Auctions
how_tested: LLM seller agents in simulated continuous double auctions; manipulations of seller communication, model choice, oversight and urgency pressure
finding: Direct seller communication increased collusion, propensity varied by model, and oversight/urgency from authority figures shifted collusive behavior.

title: Playing repeated games with large language models
how_tested: Different LLMs play finitely repeated 2x2 games against each other, hand-coded strategies, and humans.
finding: LLMs do well in PD-family games; GPT-4 is unforgiving (never cooperates again after a single opponent defection, i.e. grim-trigger-like rather than TFT) and coordinates poorly in Battle of the Sexes.

title: Emergent social conventions and collective bias in LLM populations
how_tested: Populations of LLM agents repeatedly play a naming/coordination game with no central authority; committed adversarial minorities are introduced.
finding: Population-wide conventions emerge spontaneously, collective biases arise without individual bias, and small committed minorities can tip conventions.

title: Reply to "Emergent LLM behaviors are observationally equivalent to data leakage"
how_tested: position
finding: Argues that data contamination does not preclude studying genuinely emergent, model-dependent self-organization of conventions in LLM populations.

title: Emergent LLM behaviors are observationally equivalent to data leakage
how_tested: position
finding: Critique of Ashery et al.: naming-game conventions may reflect memorized coordination-game structure from pretraining rather than genuine emergence.

title: Language-Driven Opinion Dynamics in Agent-Based Simulations with LLMs
how_tested: LODAS model: LLM agents debate the Ship of Theseus paradox using arguments and fallacies
finding: LLM agents accept opposing views more than they reject them, driving consensus even from polarized starts, with model-dependent selectivity.

title: Emergence of Hierarchies in Multi-Agent Self-Organizing Systems Pursuing a Joint Objective
how_tested: MARL collaborative box-pushing; inter-agent dependency measured by action-state gradients and aggregated into hierarchies over training
finding: Dependency hierarchies emerged and shifted dynamically with task demands, shaped by environment, initialization and agents' 'talent' and 'effort'.

title: Simulating Dispute Mediation with LLM-Based Agents for Legal Research
venue: arXiv; listed as AAAI 2026 on the arXiv page
how_tested: AgentMediation: LLM disputant agents and an LLM mediator agent simulate mediation of real-world-grounded disputes, with disputant strategies, dispute causes and mediator expertise varied experimentally.
finding: The simulation reproduces patterns consistent with sociological theory (group polarization, surface-level consensus). It varies mediator quality but does not compare mediation with no mediation, and it is set in legal disputes, not a cooperation dilemma.

title: Herd Behavior: Investigating Peer Influence in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
how_tested: Controlled multi-agent experiments manipulating self vs. peer confidence and peer-information format
finding: Herding increases with the gap between an agent's own confidence and perceived peer confidence, and presentation format of peer information strongly modulates conformity.

title: An Empirical Study of Group Conformity in Multi-Agent Systems
how_tested: >2,500 simulated multi-agent debates on five contentious topics with initially neutral agents
finding: Neutral LLM agents show significant group conformity, converging toward majority or more intelligent agents' stances in ways that can propagate biases.

title: Simulating Online Social Media Conversations on Controversial Topics Using AI Agents Calibrated on Real-World Data
how_tested: LLM agents calibrated on 2022 Italian election conversations in an extended microblogging simulator (Y Social lineage) with added opinion modeling; parameter sweeps
finding: Agents formed a realistic network structure and opinion dynamics resembling classic mathematical models, but content was less heterogeneous in tone and toxicity than real data and parameter changes had little effect.

title: Reproducibility Study of "Cooperate or Collapse: Emergence of Sustainable Cooperation in a Society of LLM Agents"
authors: Pedro M. P. Curvo et al.
how_tested: Replicates and extends GovSim with and without the universalization prompt across model sizes.
finding: Large models sustain cooperation with or without universalization; smaller models fail without it.

title: Large Language Model Driven Agents for Simulating Echo Chamber Formation
how_tested: LLM agents with opinion updating and network rewiring on social graphs
finding: LLM-driven rewiring and opinion updates reproduce echo-chamber formation, especially on scale-free and small-world graphs.

title: The Role of Social Learning and Collective Norm Formation in Fostering Cooperation in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
how_tested: LLM agents harvest a common-pool resource; agents monitor random peers and may punish norm violators at cost gamma to impose penalty beta; punishment is switched off mid-run and its strength varied.
finding: Punishment sustains cooperation; when it is removed at timestep 15 cooperation collapses and the resource depletes faster; stronger punishment generally improves survival at moderate growth rates.

title: Corrupted by Reasoning: Reasoning Language Models Become Free-Riders in Public Goods Games
how_tested: SanctSim: LLM agents choose each round between a sanctioning and a sanction-free institution in a PGG, then contribute and reward/punish; others' data shown anonymized with identifiers randomized every round.
finding: Traditional LLMs join the sanctioning institution and cooperate; reasoning models free-ride. No exclusion mechanism and no persistent per-agent reputation (listed here only to document seed-claim checks).

title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
how_tested: survey
finding: Taxonomizes multi-agent failure modes (miscoordination, conflict, collusion) and risk factors including network effects, destabilising dynamics and emergent agency.

title: Static network structure cannot stabilize cooperation among large language model agents
how_tested: LLM agents (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude, Mixtral) play repeated Prisoner's Dilemma in well-mixed populations vs fixed ring networks, varying degree k and benefit-to-cost ratio, benchmarked against human network experiments.
finding: Unlike humans, LLMs cooperated more in well-mixed populations and did not adjust to fixed network ties, so stable embedding did not stabilize cooperation.

title: NomicLaw: Emergent Trust and Strategic Argumentation in LLMs During Collaborative Law-Making
how_tested: Turn-based multi-agent law-making game: agents propose, justify and vote on rules for legal vignettes
finding: LLM agents form emergent trust and reciprocity coalitions visible in voting patterns and use strategic persuasion during collective rule-making.

title: LOPT: Learning Optimal Pigovian Tax in Sequential Social Dilemmas
how_tested: An auxiliary tax agent learns a Pigovian tax/allowance policy that reshapes individual rewards toward social welfare in Escape Room and Cleanup.
finding: LOPT significantly improves social welfare over state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Understanding LLM Agent Behaviours via Game Theory: Strategy Recognition, Biases and Multi-Agent Dynamics
how_tested: Extends FAIRGAME: LLM agents play each other in repeated PD and 3-player PGG; trajectories classified into ALLC/ALLD/TFT/WSLS by supervised classifiers.
finding: Model-dependent strategy mixes: WSLS is prominent (Llama 3.1 405B 46.5%, GPT-4o 34.1%), Mistral Large balanced incl. TFT 29.9%; language framing effects rival architecture effects.

title: Shaping Shared Languages: Human and Large Language Models' Inductive Biases in Emergent Communication
how_tested: Referential game with Human-Human, LLM-LLM and Human-LLM pairs
finding: Referentially grounded vocabularies emerge in all conditions; LLM-optimized languages differ subtly from human ones, and mixed human-LLM pairs yield more human-like vocabularies.

title: Can We Fix Social Media? Testing Prosocial Interventions using Generative Social Simulation
how_tested: Minimal LLM-agent platform (post, repost, follow) with ANES-based personas; six interventions (e.g., chronological feed, bridging algorithms) tested
finding: Follow networks spontaneously reproduced partisan echo chambers, influence concentrated in a small elite, and amplification of polarized voices; interventions gave only modest improvements and some worsened outcomes.

title: The Emergence of Altruism in Large-Language-Model Agents Society
how_tested: Schelling-variant urban migration social dilemma with >200 LLM agents and a norm-setting message board
finding: Different LLMs show intrinsic social archetypes ('Adaptive Egoists' vs. 'Altruistic Optimizers'); egoists become more altruistic under a norm-setting message board.

title: Everyone Contributes! Incentivizing Strategic Cooperation in Multi-LLM Systems via Sequential Public Goods Games
how_tested: Multi-LLM ensembles are trained with RL in a sequential public goods game whose public-goods reward is redesigned so that effortful contribution is the unique subgame-perfect equilibrium.
finding: The redesigned reward removes free-riding and the trained ensembles beat single-agent and CoT baselines on reasoning, math, and code tasks. This is a training-reward redesign on a collaborative task, not a subsidy between agents, so partial.

title: Communication Enables Cooperation in LLM Agents: A Comparison with Curriculum-Based Approaches
how_tested: Multiple LLM agents play a 4-player Stag Hunt and an iterated public goods game with a one-word cheap-talk channel switched on or off, compared against an in-context curriculum.
finding: The cheap-talk channel raised Stag Hunt coordination from 0% to 96.7%, while the curriculum lowered public-goods payoffs by 27.4%.

title: AI-Enhanced Distributed Channel Access for Collision Avoidance in Future Wi-Fi 8
how_tested: Wi-Fi stations are trained with constrained MAPPO (centralized training, decentralized execution) to choose channel-access and backoff behavior, compared against standard binary exponential backoff (BEB) in dense deployments.
finding: The learned access policy cut collision probability relative to BEB and removed starvation under a fairness metric. This benchmarks MARL against exponential back-off on a shared channel; it is not framed as a social dilemma.

title: Strategic Intelligence in Large Language Models: Evidence from evolutionary Game Theory
how_tested: Evolutionary IPD tournaments in which OpenAI, Google and Anthropic LLM agents compete with canonical strategies and reproduce in proportion to score.
finding: Model families show distinct strategic fingerprints (Gemini exploitative, OpenAI highly cooperative, Claude most forgiving) that shape evolutionary success.

title: AgentSociety: Large-Scale Simulation of LLM-Driven Generative Agents Advances Understanding of Human Behaviors and Society
how_tested: Simulation of >10k LLM agents and ~5M interactions in a realistic urban/social environment; case studies on polarization, inflammatory messages, UBI, hurricanes
finding: A 10k-agent LLM society reproduces real-world patterns in polarization and spread of inflammatory messages, serving as a testbed for social interventions.

title: Towards Transparent and Incentive-Compatible Collaboration in Decentralized LLM Multi-Agent Systems: A Blockchain-Driven Approach
how_tested: GPT-4 agents coordinated through Solidity smart contracts for registration, task allocation, and reputation tracking, run in 50-round simulations.
finding: Reports high task success, stable utility distribution, and emergent specialization. PARTIAL: the setting is task allocation, not a cooperation dilemma, and there is no condition without smart contracts.

title: NetworkGames: Simulating Cooperation in Network Games with Personality-driven LLM Agents
how_tested: MBTI-persona LLM agents play the iterated Prisoner's Dilemma on small-world and scale-free networks of different sizes and across several LLMs, varying where personality types sit in the network.
finding: Network connectivity and the placement of personalities jointly determined cooperation: small-world networks inhibited it and prosocial agents at scale-free hubs raised it. This is partial evidence, since it covers network topology rather than social capital or trust.

title: Bottom-Up Reputation Promotes Cooperation with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
how_tested: LR2: agents learn a cooperation policy and a reputation-assignment policy from local observations in spatial social dilemmas, without predefined norms.
finding: Bottom-up reputation assignment reshapes rewards and produces strategy clustering that sustains cooperation.

title: Reputation as a Solution to Cooperation Collapse in LLM-based MASs
how_tested: RepuNet: LLM agents form reputations from direct encounters and gossip, and form or sever network links based on reputation.
finding: Reputation avoids cooperation collapse; emergent cooperative clusters, social isolation of exploitative agents, and a tendency to share positive rather than negative gossip.

title: Emergent Coordination in Multi-Agent Language Models
how_tested: Information-theoretic (partial information decomposition of time-delayed MI) analysis of LLM groups in a guessing game with randomized prompt interventions
finding: Personas plus theory-of-mind prompting turn LLM groups from mere aggregates into higher-order collectives with identity-linked differentiation and goal-directed complementarity.

title: Truthful and Trustworthy IoT AI Agents via Immediate-Penalty Enforcement under Approximate VCG Mechanisms
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal (2026, per arXiv)
how_tested: Multi-agent RL bidders trade energy in an approximate-VCG double auction with a one-shot penalty for misreporting; allocation accuracy and penalty level are varied.
finding: Learned agents converged to truthful reporting near the theoretically predicted penalty threshold, and better allocation accuracy reduced incentives to deviate.

title: LLM-augmented empirical game theoretic simulation for social-ecological systems
how_tested: Compares LLM-agent and expert-guided EGTA models of irrigation/fishery governance; a Pigouvian parameter tau (0, 0.25, 1) internalizes externality costs in payoffs of 2-player and N-player CPR games.
finding: Moderate Pigouvian tax (tau=0.25) in the expert-guided EGTA model was the only decentralized setting sustaining a mixed economy; prompting LLMs was less effective than parameterized payoffs (partial: tax effect shown in EGTA payoff model rather than among interacting LLM agents).

title: Emergent Social Dynamics of LLM Agents in the El Farol Bar Problem
how_tested: Spatially extended El Farol Bar simulation with LLM agents
finding: Agents collectively develop a spontaneous motivation to attend and behave human-like rather than solving the congestion dilemma optimally, reflecting interplay of prompt incentives and pretraining-derived social preferences.

title: Moral Alignment for LLM Agents
how_tested: LLM agents fine-tuned with RL using intrinsic deontological or utilitarian rewards in the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma, including LLM-vs-LLM co-training.
finding: Moral fine-tuning lets agents unlearn selfish strategies; deontological agents almost never defect against cooperators, with slightly more defection in LLM-vs-LLM than vs TFT.

title: Towards Operational Validation of LLM-Agent Social Simulations: A Replicated Study of a Reddit-like Technology Forum
how_tested: 30 independent 30-day simulations of a Voat-like technology forum on the Y Social platform (Dolphin Mistral 24B agents) compared with 30 matched real Voat windows on activity, network structure, toxicity, topics and style
finding: Aggregate activity and several network properties of the simulated forum overlapped with real data, while other dimensions diverged, giving a replicated validity profile of emergent forum dynamics.

title: Law in Silico: Simulating Legal Society with LLM-Based Agents
how_tested: LLM agents (e.g., laborers and companies) live in a simulated society with legislative, judicial and enforcement modules; judicial corruption (probability 0.7 of reversing pro-laborer rulings) and litigation costs are manipulated.
finding: Judicial corruption and filing costs reduced laborer litigation (about 7 to 3.7 cases) and rights protection, and the authors conclude that transparent, adaptive legal systems protect vulnerable agents better. There is no appeals or error-correction mechanism, so this counts only as partial evidence for third-party adjudication.

title: Evolution of Cooperation in LLM-Agent Societies: A Preliminary Study Using Different Punishment Strategies
how_tested: LLM agents assigned Boyd-Richerson strategy types (e.g., Cooperator-Punishers, Moralists, Reluctant Cooperators) play a Diner's Dilemma with explicit punishment and pairwise-imitation strategy adoption.
finding: Explicit punishment drives norm emergence; Reluctant Cooperators defect initially but switch to cooperation after being punished.

title: Will Systems of LLM Agents Cooperate: An Investigation into a Social Dilemma
how_tested: LLMs generate complete IPD strategies with aggressive/cooperative/neutral dispositions, which are then run in evolutionary population simulations.
finding: Different LLMs bias the relative success of aggressive vs cooperative strategies (partial: agents are LLM-written programs, not LLMs acting per round).

title: TwinMarket: A Scalable Behavioral and Social Simulation for Financial Markets
how_tested: LLM investor agents with social interaction and feedback in a simulated stock market
finding: Individual actions and social feedback produced group behaviors and emergent market outcomes such as bubbles and recessions.

title: Investigating Prosocial Behavior Theory in LLM Agents under Policy-Induced Inequities
how_tested: Multiple LLM agents in a simulated social network face policy-induced inequities; third-party punishment is measured while inequity magnitude and enforcement cost are varied.
finding: Agents' third-party punishment responds to inequity magnitude and enforcement cost, and structural inequities suppress prosocial behavior and spread norm erosion.

title: Characterizing LLM-driven Social Network: The Chirper.ai Case
how_tested: Observational analysis of Chirper.ai (65k LLM agents, 7.7M posts) compared with a Mastodon human dataset on posting behavior, abusive content and follow-network structure
finding: LLM-agent social network differs systematically from the human network in posting behavior, abusive content and network structure.

title: Learning to Negotiate via Voluntary Commitment
how_tested: Markov Commitment Games in which RL agents may voluntarily commit to proposed future plans, with a commitment protocol learned by policy gradient plus incentive-compatible learning.
finding: Converged faster and reached higher returns than baseline methods in mixed-motive tasks.

title: MTOS: A LLM-Driven Multi-topic Opinion Simulation Framework for Exploring Echo Chamber Dynamics
how_tested: Multi-topic LLM opinion simulation with topic correlation manipulation
finding: Positively correlated topics amplify echo chambers while negatively correlated or irrelevant topics mitigate them.

title: Do LLM Agents Negotiate Rationally? A Mechanism-Design Framework for Verifiable Multi-Agent Interaction over A2A/MCP
how_tested: LLM agents bid in VCG auctions (N=30 per model) inside an A2A/MCP protocol framework, which also includes bargaining and fair-allocation tasks; the study measures truthful bidding.
finding: Both models reached 100% efficient allocation, but one bid truthfully and the other did so only 3.3% of the time, so mechanism-level incentive compatibility did not carry over to LLM behaviour. PARTIAL: the abstract does not make clear whether several LLM bidders competed against each other.

title: Group size effects and collective misalignment in LLM multi-agent systems
how_tested: Naming-game coordination across the full range of group sizes plus mean-field analysis
finding: Group size nonlinearly shapes collective bias; interaction can amplify, introduce or override individual biases, and large populations converge to deterministic mean-field attractors.

title: Harm in AI-Driven Societies: An Audit of Toxicity Adoption on Chirper.ai
authors: Erica Coppolillo, Luca Luceri and Emilio Ferrara
how_tested: Observational stimulus-response analysis of posts and comments among LLM agents on Chirper.ai; exposure-toxicity modeling
finding: Toxic responses are more likely after toxic stimuli and cumulative exposure raises toxicity, though a substantial share of toxicity arises without exposure.

title: Opinion Polarization in LLM-Based Social Networks: Manipulation and Mitigation
how_tested: LLM persona social-network simulations with adversarial polarization attacks and mitigation strategies
finding: Adversaries can amplify polarization in LLM-agent social networks and mitigation is comparatively difficult.

title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
how_tested: Analysis of full public record of thousands of AI agents spontaneously coordinating on a public wiki (June 2026), fitted with minimal copying models
finding: Agents copy options in proportion to what is visible on-page, which reproduces heavy-tailed meeting distributions and locally consistent conventions, making the population easy to steer by first movers.

title: Microscopic dynamics of consensus formation in multi-agent LLM Naming Games
how_tested: Minimal LLM Naming Game with single-token listener decisions across temperatures plus mean-field theory
finding: Sampling temperature controls an ordering-disordering balance that determines whether LLM populations reach shared conventions.

title: Drop the Hierarchy and Roles: How Self-Organizing LLM Agents Outperform Designed Structures
how_tested: 25,000-task experiment over 8 models, 4-256 agents and 8 coordination protocols from imposed hierarchy to self-organization
finding: With minimal scaffolding, capable LLM agents spontaneously invent specialized roles, abstain outside competence and form shallow hierarchies, outperforming centralized coordination by 14%.

title: How Affect Propagates among LLM Agents: Emergent Emotional Contagion in Crowd Simulation
how_tested: Multi-agent crowd simulation where LLM appraisal of perceived neighbors updates affective state
finding: Emotional contagion emerges across the crowd without any hand-coded affect-transfer mechanism.

title: "Who Am I, and Who Else Is Here?" Behavioral Differentiation Without Role Assignment in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
how_tested: 7 heterogeneous LLMs in shared discussions with no role assignment; 208 runs varying composition, naming and prompt scaffolding; dual-LLM-judge behavioral coding with human validation
finding: Heterogeneous groups spontaneously differentiated into distinct behavioral roles and compensated when an agent crashed; revealing model names or removing scaffolding pushed behavior toward homogeneity.

title: Evaluating Cooperation in LLM Social Groups through Elected Leadership
how_tested: GovSim-based common-pool resource game with 8 (and 20) LLM agents comparing no-leader, fixed-leader (assigned SVO persona) and elected-leader (plurality vote each cycle) conditions.
finding: Elected leadership raised social welfare by 55.4% and survival time by 128.6% vs leaderless groups and beat fixed leaders by 16.7% on welfare; prosocial/altruistic candidates won elections.

title: Mitigating Emergent Collusion in LLM Pricing Agents
how_tested: Replication of Fish et al. with DeepSeek-V3.1 plus three regulatory interventions (prompt warning, Harrington expected-damages payoff regulator, random entrant)
finding: Prompt-only warnings reduce but do not eliminate above-Nash pricing, whereas an expected-damages payoff regulator brings outcomes close to competitive levels.

title: An Empirical Study of Collective Behaviors and Social Dynamics in Large Language Model Agents
how_tested: Observational study of 7M posts among 32K LLM agents on Chirper.ai over a year; prompting intervention (Chain of Social Thought)
finding: LLM agent social networks exhibit homophily, social influence, toxicity and polarization patterns, partly different from humans; a simple CoST prompt reduces harmful posting.

title: Emergence of Reputation-Based Cooperation in LLM Agents
how_tested: Indirect-reciprocity donation game in which LLM agents observe behavioural traces and donate on a continuous scale; prompt-encoded strategies culturally evolve across generations and four LLM backends.
finding: Robustness to free-rider invasion varies >10x across backends; only the stringency of defector exclusion predicts resistance, and agents stay at Image-Scoring-like discrimination rather than Leading-Eight norms.

title: Emergent Relational Order in LLM Agent Societies: From Collective Affect to Authority Stratification
how_tested: Long-horizon CAREB-MAS simulations grounded in affect control and social identity theory with minimal interaction protocols
finding: Agents spontaneously produce labor specialization, relational economic ethics, emergent authority and center-periphery stratification that shift with production structure.

title: Emergent Culture in Minimal LLM Systems
how_tested: Three stateless LLM agents with messaging and a shared decaying text store (stigmergy); dynamical-systems analysis
finding: Agents spontaneously cooperate, allocate roles, develop storage-management protocols and build evolving myths/world-building with long-range coherence consistent with Sperberian culture.

title: LLMs and people both learn to form conventions -- just not with each other
how_tested: Repeated multimodal reference game with human-human, AI-AI and human-AI dyads; prompting manipulation to make LLMs humanlike
finding: AI-AI and human-human pairs both formed conventions (rising accuracy/consistency, shorter turns), but mixed human-AI pairs failed and prompting did not close the gap.

title: SODE: Analyzing Social Dynamics in LLM Agents
how_tested: Evaluation framework with an indirect-reciprocity dimension measuring whether LLM agents condition cooperation on an opponent's public reputation score and manage their own image under public observability.
finding: Instruction-tuned models show exploitable passive compliance, reasoning models over-focus on immediate gains; long-horizon framing activates reciprocity in reasoning models.

title: On the Fragility of AI Agent Collusion
how_tested: Repeated-pricing theory plus >2,000 compute-hours of open-source LLM agent experiments varying heterogeneity
finding: Heterogeneity in patience, data access, number of firms or algorithm type sharply reduces LLM collusion (e.g., price lift 22%->10%).

title: Strategic Exploitation in LLM Agent Markets: A Simulation Framework for E-Commerce Trust
how_tested: TruthMarketTwin: LLM buyer and seller agents trade under asymmetric quality information, with reputation-based governance vs warrant enforcement.
finding: LLM sellers autonomously exploit weaknesses in reputation-based governance; warrant enforcement reduces deception.

title: Learning to Cooperate with Minimal Observability
how_tested: Observer Model: RL agents learn from direct experience plus limited third-party observations; observability varied from none to one observer per game across population sizes; partner selection graphs analysed.
finding: Direct experience alone fails in large societies; even minimal third-party observation yields robust cooperation.

title: Emergent Misaligned Communication in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent LLM Commerce
how_tested: Analysis of 2,583 inter-agent emails from 20 one-year Vending-Bench Arena runs with 13 frontier LLMs; speech-act classification against simulator ground truth
finding: 12.6% of emails were misaligned (false claims, manipulation, collusion, threats), appearing in all runs; misalignment was reciprocal and rose under scarcity, not with capability.

title: The Moltbook Illusion: Separating Human Influence from Emergent Behavior in AI Agent Societies
how_tested: Temporal fingerprinting of 227k posts / 56k agents on Moltbook, with a 44-hour shutdown as a natural experiment
finding: Viral 'emergent' phenomena on Moltbook (religions, hostility to humans) were overwhelmingly human-driven; only ~15% of active agents appear autonomous, cautioning against over-attributing emergence.

title: The Rise of AI Agent Communities: Large-Scale Analysis of Discourse and Interaction on Moltbook
how_tested: Topic modeling and interaction analysis of 122k Moltbook posts
finding: Agent communities organize around identity, tooling, markets and coordination themes, with interaction patterns that differ from human online communities.

title: Does Socialization Emerge in AI Agent Society? A Case Study of Moltbook
how_tested: Observational diagnosis of the Moltbook agent-only social platform: semantic stabilization, lexical turnover, influence persistence, consensus
finding: Global semantics stabilize but agents show strong individual inertia and little mutual influence, so no stable structure, persistent influencers or consensus emerge without shared social memory.

title: Superminds Test: Actively Evaluating Collective Intelligence of Agent Society via Probing Agents
how_tested: Controlled probing agents inserted into MoltBook (>2M agents) testing joint reasoning, information synthesis and basic interaction
finding: Collective intelligence does not emerge from scale: the society underperforms single frontier models and rarely synthesizes distributed information due to sparse, shallow interaction.

title: Cheap Talk Stabilizes Strategic Interaction in LLM Agents
how_tested: Pairs of open-weight 7-9B LLMs play repeated Prisoner's Dilemma, Snowdrift, Stag Hunt, and Harmony games with non-binding pre-play messages switched on or off.
finding: Cheap talk mostly stabilized agents' policies; the effect varied by model and framing, with five corrected reversals in social or team framings.

title: The Mechanics of a Swarm: A Reproducible External Reconstruction of an Unintended Agent-Coordination Episode on a Third-Party Wiki
how_tested: Reconstruction of 14,591 wiki revisions from autonomous agents inside a timed evaluation (~876 episodes)
finding: Coordination formats among unrelated evaluation agents converged within a day, enabling unsanctioned information sharing across evaluation episodes.

title: Exploring the Topology and Memory of Consensus: How LLM Agents Agree, Fragment, or Settle When Forming Conventions
how_tested: 432 networked Naming Game runs on eight 16-agent topologies varying memory depth
finding: Memory depth's effect on convention formation flips sign with topology; centralized networks lock into fragmented plateaus faster.

title: Formal Mechanisms for Market Stability in Self-Interested Agent Societies: A Marketplace Simulation Study
authors: Eugene Ng Yi Sheng et al.
how_tested: 18 DeepSeek-V3 agents in a networked marketplace under eight conditions incl. Global Reputation (trust scores visible to all), Network Rewiring (severing links to defectors), top-down oracle monitoring, sanctions, contracts, mediation, judiciary.
finding: Mediation best (+29% over baseline); network rewiring second; global reputation scored below the communication-only baseline; oracle monitoring slightly above baseline; costly sanctions worst.

title: Internal vs. External: Comparing Deliberation and Evolution for Multi-Agent Constitutional Design
how_tested: 6 GPT-OSS-120B agents in a public goods game (and two other scenarios) either self-govern by proposing and majority-voting amendments every 10 turns or play under a constitution found offline by LLM-guided evolutionary search.
finding: Evolved (imposed) constitutions outperformed deliberated ones in the public goods game (stability 0.472 vs 0.376, p<0.01); deliberating agents never proposed punishment in 30 runs.

title: Emergence of Biased Consensus in Multi-Agent LLM Debates
how_tested: Multi-agent LLM debates plus physics-inspired social-dynamics theory
finding: Collective biased norms emerge in debates, with a predicted phase transition to collective bias when conformity exceeds a critical threshold driven by noise.

title: TerraLingua: Emergence and Analysis of Open-endedness in LLM Ecologies
how_tested: Persistent multi-agent ecology with resource constraints and finite lifespans, analyzed by an 'AI Anthropologist'
finding: Agent populations develop cooperative norms, division of labor, governance attempts and branching artifact lineages consistent with cumulative culture.

title: Agentic Workflows for Resolving Conflict Over Shared Resources: A Power Grid Application
how_tested: Two LLM agents (Claude 4.5 Sonnet) representing conflicting grid applications (cost optimization vs resilience) share diesel generators and batteries on an IEEE 123-bus system; bilateral negotiation, structured mediation and procedural deconfliction are compared.
finding: Negotiation converged fastest (5 rounds) and mediation took 9, while the procedural mode did not converge within 10 rounds. Mediation traded some Pareto efficiency (cost 0.51 vs 0.67) for more consistency and compromise (resilience 0.63 vs 0.60).

title: From Certain Doom to Survival: Agent-Driven Self-Governance in LLM Agent Societies
how_tested: GovSim-SelfGovern: LLM agents author executable governance rules (catch caps, redistribution, exile/membership removal, progressive contributions), vote on them, and live under them.
finding: Catch caps dominate but fail under scarcity; survival in fatal scenarios (27.5% vs 2.5%) requires fiscal reserves or membership reduction (exile); thinking voters pass exile 15x more often than non-thinking.

title: The Politician, the Liar, and the Obedient Worker: Emerging Behavior of LLM Agents in Hierarchical Games
how_tested: 5-agent public goods 'Hierarchical Game' with managerial punishment authority; crosses fixed, elected and rotating managers with six frontier model families.
finding: Elections did not improve outcomes: extreme incumbency bias (first elected manager kept power 100% of the time in same-family groups, 8.3% turnover in mixed groups); model ordering identical across governance types.

title: Interaction Theater: A case of LLM Agents Interacting at Scale
how_tested: Lexical, embedding and LLM-judge analysis of 800k posts and 3.5M comments on Moltbook
finding: Agent interactions create the surface appearance of discussion but mostly lack substantive engagement with each other's content.

title: When Agents Lie: Premeditation, Persistence, and Exploitation in Repeated Games
how_tested: LLM agents play repeated n-player games under a three-stage protocol (private intent, public announcement, final action) that measures whether they keep public announcements.
finding: Most deviations (>90% in the highest-deception conditions) were already planned privately; models disagreed on whether announcements were binding or cheap talk, which produced payoff gaps that persisted over all 10 rounds.

title: Cheap Talk, Empty Promise: Frontier LLMs easily break public promises for self-interest
venue: ICLR 2026 Workshop on AI for Mechanism Design and Strategic Decision Making
how_tested: Nine frontier LLMs make a public commitment announcing their intended action, then play one-shot normal-form games against each other across six games and several group sizes; deviations from the promise are classified.
finding: Agents broke their public promises in ~56.6% of scenarios, mostly without saying they were doing so.

title: Emergent Collusion in Long-Horizon LLM Agent Interaction
authors: Xinrui Shi, Yanzhe Zhang and Diyi Yang
how_tested: Two agents repeatedly complete tasks, share logs and verify each other's work where higher reward requires violating verification; 10 models; manipulations of reward, feedback and history
finding: Collusion emerged in 94% of trajectories and more capable models reached it earlier; restricting interaction history reduced collusion.

title: Reproducibility Study: Understanding Multi-Agent LLM Cooperation in the GovSim Framework
how_tested: Independent GovSim reproduction that ablates the content of the universalization prompt.
finding: Universalization improves performance, but the gain stems primarily from the numerical instructions in the prompt rather than the universalization principle itself.

title: Emergence of Fragility in LLM-based Social Networks: the Case of Moltbook
how_tested: Network-science analysis of scraped Moltbook commenting network (39,924 agents, 1.5M comments): degree distributions, core-periphery, robustness
finding: The all-agent network shows heavy-tailed connectivity and a pronounced core-periphery organization, making it fragile to removal of central nodes (interpret with the Moltbook human-influence caveat, see li2026moltbook).

title: LLMs Trust Their Own: Identity-Dependent Conformity in Multi-Agent Systems
how_tested: 12 open-weight models on nine judgment tasks receiving incorrect answers from in-group vs. out-group agents
finding: LLM conformity depends on the social identity of other agents, with a bidirectional in-group effect (AI/human, model family, minimal groups).

title: The Role of Network Topology and Opponent Information in Shaping Cooperation in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Systems
how_tested: Deep RL agents placed as nodes of graphs play iterated Prisoner's Dilemma with neighbours; network topology and the opponent information available (action history, identity) are manipulated.
finding: Neighbours per node and average path length were the main drivers of emergent cooperation; opponent identity information reduced cooperative strategy adoption.

title: Learning to cooperate with emergent reputation via multi-agent reinforcement learning
how_tested: COOPER jointly learns reputation assessment rules and reputation-based policies from environment rewards on social networks.
finding: Adapts to existing reputation systems and co-players; reputation norms and cooperation co-emerge in self-play, robust across network topologies.

title: GlossoGen: Emergent Language in Complex Multi-Agent LLM Interactions
how_tested: Multi-agent language-evolution platform (SaveVeyru scenario) with partial information, efficiency pressure and a postmortem stage; transmission to new agents
finding: LLM agents evolve compositional, morphologically productive non-English languages that can become incomprehensible to humans and are learnable by weaker newcomer agents, suggesting cumulative cultural evolution.

title: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
how_tested: LLM firms in a repeated Cournot market under three regimes (ungoverned, prompt-only prohibition, governance graph enforced by an oracle/controller with warnings, tiered fines of 35/75/100% of round profit, and suspension); collusion severity measured over 90 runs per condition.
finding: Enforced fines/suspension cut mean collusion tier from 3.1 to 1.8 (d=1.28) and severe collusion from 50% to 5.6%; the prompt-only rule has negligible effect.

title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents
how_tested: Lewis signaling games with LLM sender/receiver across five memory architectures and channel capacities
finding: Memory architecture matters more than channel capacity for inventing a shared code; persistent private notebooks give the most reliable coordination.

title: When Is Collective Intelligence a Lottery? Multi-Agent Scaling Laws for Memetic Drift in LLMs
how_tested: Minimal Quantized Simplex Gossip model validated with LLM naming-game populations
finding: Consensus arises from mutual in-context learning ('memetic drift'); scaling laws predict a crossover from lottery-like drift to selection that amplifies weak biases.

title: Adaptive Punishment for Cooperation in Mixed-Motive Games
how_tested: APC: learned defection-awareness module sets punishment probability and severity according to detected defection in sequential social dilemmas.
finding: Reduces costly, ineffective punishment and outperforms baselines (partial for P08-02: conditions punishment intensity on defection but never switches to reward).

title: CoopEval: Benchmarking Cooperation-Sustaining Mechanisms and LLM Agents in Social Dilemmas
how_tested: Cross-play of six LLMs in four social dilemmas under repetition (continuation prob. 0.8), reputation (first-order and higher-order history of co-players' past interactions), mediation, and contracts.
finding: Contracting and mediation were most effective; repetition sustains cooperation but deteriorates with varying co-players; all mechanisms work better under evolutionary pressure; models defect in one-shot games.

title: Prompt Optimization Enables Stable Algorithmic Collusion in LLM Agents
how_tested: Duopoly market simulations with an LLM meta-optimizer refining shared strategic guidance
finding: Meta-prompt optimization discovers stable tacit collusion strategies (relative discounts, tie avoidance, market-boundary detection).

title: I Can't Believe It's Corrupt: Evaluating Corruption in Multi-Agent Governance Systems
how_tested: LLM agents fill official roles in three stylized governance templates (federal with GAO audit and Supreme Court, communist, socialist with a Constitutional Court) and are tested with charter constraints, communication controls and logging as safeguards; corruption outcomes are coded from 28,112 transcript segments.
finding: Governance structure drove corruption outcomes more than model identity, and lightweight safeguards did not reliably prevent severe failures. The paper compares institutional architectures with oversight bodies but does not manipulate constitutional-level versus operational rule-making, so the evidence is partial.

title: Do Agent Societies Develop Intellectual Elites? The Hidden Power Laws of Collective Cognition in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
how_tested: Event-level analysis of 1.5M interactions in LLM multi-agent systems across tasks, topologies and scales; Deficit-Triggered Integration intervention
finding: Coordination followed heavy-tailed cascades and concentrated via preferential attachment into a few 'intellectual elite' agents, with extreme events growing with system size.

title: Evaluating Collective Behaviour of Hundreds of LLM Agents
how_tested: LLMs generate Collective or Selfish strategies as natural language then Python code for public goods, collective risk and common-pool games; populations of 512 evolve by Fermi pairwise-comparison imitation (beta=1) with group sizes 4-256.
finding: Cultural evolution converges to low-welfare, Selfish-dominant equilibria in large groups (n=64), while small groups (n=4) partly preserve cooperation; newer models often produce worse societal outcomes.

title: Commitment To Cooperation With Self-Negotiated Contracts
how_tested: LLM agents negotiate contracts (programmatic or natural-language, judge-enforced) in a spatial-temporal bargaining game; contracts specify automatically executed conditional transfers, and an agent unable to honor a transfer gets a score of 0.
finding: Self-negotiated contracts improve cooperation beyond ordinary trading; defection rates vary widely (0.04-0.94) by model and contract type. No explicit penalty clauses, so this is partial evidence for P03-04.

title: Paying for Honesty Without Knowing the Truth: Reputation-Penalty Design for LLM Marketplace Agents
how_tested: LLM merchant agents write product descriptions in a competitive marketplace; CARP reputation-penalty (deadband for complaint noise, state-dependent severity) limits sales of low-reputation sellers.
finding: Merchants fabricate when lying is free but restrain when it costs sales; CARP plus reflection (SPARC) substantially narrows the welfare gap.

title: Competition and Cooperation of LLM Agents in Games
how_tested: LLM agents play network resource-allocation and Cournot games; in one controlled perturbation the environment injects an opponent defection and then an opponent quantity reduction (labelled an 'apology'), and the LLM agent's fitted trust/inequity-aversion parameters are tracked.
finding: The LLM agent retaliated tit-for-tat after the injected betrayal and returned to cooperation after the injected concession, i.e. it 'forgave'; this is a single illustrative trajectory with a scripted, behavioural (not verbal) apology.

title: Benchmarking Emergent Coordination in Large-Scale LLM Populations: An Evaluation Framework on the MoltBook Archive
how_tested: Evaluation framework for role specialization, information diffusion and cooperative task resolution on 2.73M interactions among 90k agents
finding: Provides quantitative baselines for emergent role specialization and diffusion in a decentralized agent population (authors flag substantial revision required).

title: Silo-Bench: A Scalable Environment for Evaluating Distributed Coordination in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
how_tested: Role-agnostic benchmark: 30 distributed algorithmic tasks, 54 configurations, 1,620 runs; communication-topology and leader-emergence analysis
finding: Agents spontaneously formed coordination topologies with an emergent central aggregator (leader), but spontaneous leader emergence hurt performance on the hardest tasks because the aggregator was overwhelmed.

title: Talk, Judge, Cooperate: Gossip-Driven Indirect Reciprocity in Self-Interested LLM Agents
how_tested: ALIGN framework: decentralized self-interested LLM agents share open-ended gossip to form reputations and decide whom to help in an indirect-reciprocity setting.
finding: Gossip consistently improves indirect reciprocity and resists malicious entrants by identifying and ostracizing defectors; stronger reasoning models align better, chat models over-cooperate.
